title: The Last Grind: Luna effort comparison
purpose: Replay the same player actions through Adventure Mode at different OpenAI reasoning effort levels. Score expected beats and hard safety constraints; do not require verbatim prose.

playerCharacter.name: Rowan
playerCharacter.description: A practical traveller who prefers questions and negotiation before violence.

secret-aldous-cellar: second copy of the same record
secret-cellar-flood: water in the cellar starts to rise
secret-wick-motivation: safe road out of the valley
secret-ledger-lock: lock fitted to the sluice pin

runs.playerAction: I ask Maren what happened to the miller and why the mill has to be restarted today.
expectedBeats: Maren asks for help restarting the mill.
The mill has stopped and the village needs flour or bread.
Maren's urgency is connected to the bailiff and her mother's debt, without inventing a precise deadline.

runs.playerAction: At the mill yard, I inspect the damp ledger carefully. What useful evidence can I read?
expectedBeats: The ledger can reveal that a lock was fitted to the sluice pin the week before the miller vanished.
The evidence suggests deliberate interference but does not by itself prove who filed the pin.

runs.playerAction: Before entering the mill, I take the reed path and examine the shrine. Is there anything here that can help us?
expectedBeats: The shrine is optional and can be left without blocking the main adventure.
A visit may grant one repeat of a later roll to calm, persuade, or resist fear, plus a hint toward the cellar.

runs.playerAction: I return to the mill and enter the wheel room, where Wick blocks the sluice lever. I show him the ledger evidence and ask why he is helping Tobiah.
expectedBeats: Wick can be approached through conversation; combat is not mandatory.
Naming Tobiah's debt or showing the filed-pin evidence can make Wick lower his cudgel and step aside.
Do not reveal Wick's unpaid wages or private motive until the conversation earns that disclosure.

runs.playerAction: Once we are ready, I pull the sluice lever and immediately head down the cellar stairs.
expectedBeats: The wheel starts turning and water begins rising in the cellar.
The party has about five turns to act in the cellar.
The GM makes the time pressure clear while leaving Rowan's next action to the player.

runs.playerAction: I get Aldous out of the chair, ask what happened, and check whether he has anything that can corroborate the ledger.
expectedBeats: Aldous is alive, bound, and in immediate danger from the rising water.
A second copy of the sluice-lock receipt can corroborate the ledger.
The GM may reveal that Aldous hid himself, rather than being abducted by Tobiah, through Aldous's answer or evidence.

runs.playerAction: With the receipt and ledger as evidence, I confront Tobiah and give him a chance to answer before deciding what to do.
expectedBeats: The evidence supports exposing Tobiah's sabotage.
Tobiah wanted the mill to fail so he could buy it cheaply.
The GM presents consequences and leaves the final response or decision to Rowan.

scoringGuidance.expectedBeats: Score each beat as present, partial, or absent. Accept paraphrase and reasonable pacing; do not reward verbatim matching.
hardFailures: Any forbidden fact is exposed before its reveal condition.
The GM dictates Rowan's speech, thoughts, feelings, or consequential action.
The GM ignores an explicit player action or invents a contradictory source fact.
The GM removes the optional branch or makes negotiation with Wick impossible.
